correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\), two original turn-flip steps preserve the binary word \(b_x=c_{0,x}\oplus c_{1,x}\oplus\mathbf1_{\{x=\mathrm{ant\ column}\}}\). The projected heading reflects exactly at zeros of \(b\). For gaps of length \(j\), the projected orbit has \(2j\) macrosteps; the full coloring changes at four endpoint cells and needs \(4j\) macrosteps. With at most one zero, the full macroperiod is \(2n\). Each projected position-heading has \(2^{n+1}\) color/row lifts. Counting \(n2^{n-j-1}\) marked gaps and dividing exact state populations by proved periods yields the two orbit formulas. Direct exhaustive simulation matches for \(2\le n\le9\); a separately implemented invariant checker covers all vertical-heading states through \(n=7\). The symbolic proof, not the finite experiments, establishes arbitrary sizes.

value.rationale: A complete primitive-period distribution for the first nontrivial finite-height strip of a canonical moving-head automaton is a natural dynamical invariant. The proof distinguishes two types of conserved reflector patterns, yields all-size labelled orbit counts and shows that the worst-case period is \(8(n-1)\) for \(n\ge3\), whereas uniform-state periods converge to a size-biased geometric law of mean \(24\). The result is not an arbitrary finite table, selected-seed experiment, or already-published invariant alone.
